newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes down, ignores Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes down, ignores Wall Street.

text.p: The Czech PX50 lost early gains to close slightly lower on Wednesday with analysts saying the Czech market had simply ignored strong overnight gains on Wall Street and subsequent surges on west European bourses.
"Hungary is probably linked more to Western Europe...but the Czech market, with the capital market problems and the flooding, will not be linked in an immediate way," said Eugene Klerk.
The PX50 fell 0.3 percent to 501.2 with Komercni Banka falling steadily throughout the day to close down 17 crowns to 1,605.
Klerk, an analyst at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, said Komercni may still move further down but that it could soon become attractive to speculative investors.
"You may see some speculators come in to Komercni Banka but there is still some downside...I expect the stock to stabilise at a minimum of 1,550," he said.
Overall, activity was higher than in recent sessions with turnover at 1.4 billion crowns.
